title: Dark Pattern Audit Mechanism Verdict (v1)
description: Manually-ingested LLM responses (Stage 2) for one episode -- written by journey/mechanism_verdict_ingest.py (the ingest-response CLI) into episode.mechanism_verdict. episode.v2.schema.json's own mechanism_verdict field stays freeform (additionalProperties: true, {} until Phase 4) so existing episodes never fail v2 validation; THIS schema is the strict, standalone contract for the {entries:[...], computed_output:{...}} shape ingest-response/build-output actually write, validated separately -- the same pattern group_evidence.v1.schema.json uses for group_evidence.json. One entry per (role, attribute) pair; attribute is null for triage/coordinator. Re-ingesting the same (role, attribute) REPLACES its prior entry rather than appending a duplicate. computed_output is written by build_output.py (journey/episode_output_builder.py) -- the generated, presentation-layer {overall, regions, verdicts} document, never hand-authored -- and is optional: absent until build-output has run at least once for this episode.

attribute.description: Null for triage/coordinator (whole-episode roles); one of the 7 attribute ids for role=attribute.

model_name.description: Supplied by the operator at ingest time (build-payload/response_schema.json never asks the model to self-report this) -- e.g. "claude-opus-4-8".

prompt_version.description: Read from the manifest.json build-payload wrote alongside this response's response_schema.json, not re-derived, so it traces to the exact prompt the human was actually shown.

raw_response.description: The exact parsed JSON the operator pasted in, verbatim -- already validated against the response_schema.json build-payload wrote for this (episode, role[, attribute]), and (when it has an evidence_pointers field) checked for step_ids that actually exist in this episode. Never transformed or normalized before storage.

confidence.description: Always null today: the coordinator's pattern_combinations response has no confidence field to draw from (deliberately removed in an earlier session), so likely_pattern is gated on the region's own finding_strength instead of a fabricated number -- see journey/episode_output_builder.py's module docstring.

Region.description: The findings view: one entry per ui_region that had >=1 fired or unsure attribute, built by journey/episode_output_builder.py::build_regions() from `verdicts` alone. A region with everything "no"/"not_assessable" never appears here.

representative_element.description: Selector of the highest-severity fired element in this region; the first unsure element's selector if nothing fired here.

total_regions_examined.description: Every distinct region signals/ui_regions.py tagged on any captured element this episode, INCLUDING clean ones -- the false-positive/discrimination signal. Clean regions are counted here, never listed individually.

Overall.description: The honestly-scoped headline -- computed from `regions`/`verdicts`, never a hand-authored summary.

coverage_limited.description: True when >=3 of 7 attributes are not_assessable or stubbed_pending_stage2 -- verdict and summary must not overstate confidence past this.

ComputedOutput.description: Written by build_output.py / journey/episode_output_builder.py -- generated wholesale from episode.attributes.results and episode.mechanism_verdict.entries every run (idempotent full replace, same convention as episode.attributes and episode.evidence). Exactly three top-level sections: verdicts is the flat evaluation currency (source of truth); regions and overall are both COMPUTED from it, never hand-authored.

verdicts.description: One authoritative verdict per attribute (attribute_agents.base.ATTRIBUTES order) -- the ingested Stage-2 LLM entry when one exists for that attribute, else the code agent's own result. Unfiltered: includes verdict=="no", "unsure", and "not_assessable" too.
